newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish finmin wd prefer punt closer to ERM mid-poinT.
newsitem.headline: Irish finmin wd prefer punt closer to ERM mid-poinT.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said that he was "somewhat concerned" at the strength of the Irish pound in the ERM grid and would prefer to be closer to the punt's mid-point in the grid.

"We are trading within the band and trading relatively comfortably within it. We would prefer if we were closer to the medium point," he told Reuters Financial Television in an interview broadcast on Tuesday.

The punt has been trading at the top of the ERM grid for months, well above most of the other currencies and not far from its 15 percent limit. By 0845 GMT, it was 10.7 percent above the French franc, the weakest currency.
Quinn said Ireland's strong links with the British market had prompted the markets to push the Irish pound higher in tandem with a soaring sterling.
"I don't know how long that sterling position is going to last but we are comfortable within the band," he said.

Quinn declined to say at what point things would become uncomfortable but said: "We are anxious to ensure that we maintain our present position and that it doesn't go any further or go in a direction that would cause us difficulty."
Asked if he was concerned about inflation, Quinn said recent data showed that strong economic growth was not causing inflationary pressures.
March consumer price data, released last week, showed prices rose just 0.1 percent on February, he said.
